newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed, shrug off politics.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed, shrug off politics.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Tuesday as the market shrugged off news of the resignation of Justice Minister Elias Jassan and kept its attention focussed on U.S. markets.
Local bonds were slightly lower while Argentine Brady debt was boosted by gains mainly in U.S. stocks.
"The market has important support levels," said a trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/8 at 94 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was down $0.04 at 121.11.
Another trader explained that "for now" the market was paying little attention to the political impact of a scandal involving a businessman who is under police investigation in a murder case.

Jassan admitted last week he had received more than 100 phone calls from the businessman, Alfredo Yabran, after first denying he knew him. Interior Minister Carlos Corach has also said he has had contact with Yabran.
"I think politics and the economy are completely separate so there is no impact on markets," added the second trader. But, "I would lighten up my positions a little into cash."
Call money was flat at 5.70 percent.
